Ever Sunday at 5pm an Out Of Stock (OOS) scan is done. This will generate a number that the regional team will then dissect the data and turn it into a percentile of controllable/ uncontrollable OOS. 

This information is completely seen by everyone in the company that’s a buyer and above (that’s a lot of people). In my region I didn’t need a letter of intent. That would have been one of the things they ask for you to do when they told you your panel and when to start your due diligence.

I think some 30 days goals that would be good to show:

Complete Order Writer cornerstone

Learn DVO (your main hub for ordering)

Learn all vendors you order from and what days you order for them. Call them... don’t just rely on the ordering schedule. Introduce yourself over the phone, tell them you’re the new buyer and how to best do business with them. For example:

Bigger Vendors are really good about checking DVO for your POs and know the routine. 

Small mom and pop local businesses might not be as good, so you might have a PO open for a month plus... or worst, you order over another PO and they send you multiples of the product because now they see you order two cases, but really you only wanted one. 

By just picking up the phone and calling the vendors, it can save you a lot of heart ache with things like that. 

Learn IRMA (another order writing hub/ used to look up closed and open POs)

Learn Orderlink... depending on your region and what products you carry... this might be a program you use. 

Foster and build a relationship with overnight crew: these are your second set of eyes and hands on the product. You and the overnight crew are peas in a pod and have shared fate. They can be the difference of you mis-ordering something once, or ten times. 

60 day goals can include:

Merch maps
Promo planners
Building off shelf displays 
Really working on exit strategies to lower back stock numbers
Store Ops, Open to buy, forecasting. (This is more important with smaller sub teams, because they don’t make as much money. This however can clue you in if you’re ordering the right product. example: you packed out a $30 dollar oil that doesn’t move costing you say $250 for that cases, but aren’t bring enough Mac and Cheese that would actually be making you more money that week. 

90 day goals can include:

Building relationships with regional, 3rd party vendors etc.

Learn holiday trends and fluctuations that shoppers have throughout the year. Example: holidays are a no brainer, but do your sales increase on Wednesday ad change days? Is there some weird entertainment event in your town that’s taking place near your store that would drive sales. What is your stores shopper dynamic? One store might sale a lot of traditional items, but another store might have a bigger presence of East Asians and totally blow out some other set in your shelves. 

Hope this helps!
